gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (JE-1000D) ships with Energy Saving Mode on, which turns off all outputs after 12 hours when nothing is plugged in or the load is at or below a set value. Jackery says the mode can be switched off but the AC/DC output time cannot be set in the app.
standout_why: I checked the two rival pages ChatGPT cited and the two other top results. The cited ones are wattfort.com/guides/power-station-electric-blanket and blackoutwise.com/power-stations/jackery-explorer-1000-v2/electric-blanket. The other two are runtimemath.com/how-long-will-a-power-station-run-an-electric-blanket and testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket. None of them mentions a power station turning off its own outputs when the load is low. WattFort covers only the blanket side: Sunbeam's auto-off timer and Sunbeam's warning against inverters. BlackoutWise assumes a 50% duty cycle and a 0.85 loss factor, with no shutdown behaviour. RuntimeMath and TestedWatts mention only blanket auto-off. Our current Dealectric page already says in general terms that some stations switch AC off at low load and names BLUETTI's ECO mode. So the general idea is not new to our page. What is new is the Jackery 1000 v2's default and its 12-hour timer, and Jackery's 18 W standby figure.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's #2 pick, the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, rather than ruling it out. Energy Saving Mode is on out of the box, but the 12-hour timer is longer than an 8–10 h night, and the mode can be turned off. The blanket's low draw while its thermostat is off should not cut power in the middle of a normal night. The bigger runtime hit is the 18 W standby Jackery lists. Over 10 h that is 180 Wh, about 17% of the 1,070 Wh battery. ChatGPT's '≈12 h at 75 W' leaves it out (arithmetic: 1,070 × 0.85 ≈ 910 Wh; 910 / (75 + 18) ≈ 9.8 h, not 12 h). For the BLUETTI AC180 (ChatGPT's #1), the deciding question is ECO mode: whether its delay can be as short as 1–4 h and its threshold above a blanket's thermostat-off draw. I could not open a readable official source for that (see unsourced), so the page should tell AC180 owners to turn AC ECO off for overnight blanket use rather than quote numbers.
